description.p: NowCaption shows live captions for videos, calls, streams and games, or for your microphone. It is made for people who are deaf or hard of hearing, and for anyone who wants to read what is being said.
Speech is recognised on your own computer. Audio never leaves it, no account is needed, and it works offline. NowCaption currently understands English only.

ul.li: Punctuation and capital letters, written as people speak
Streaming captions that update as people speak
Light on the processor, and idle while everything is quiet
Floats above other windows on KDE Plasma, Hyprland and Sway
Adjustable text size and background, and a transcript you can copy or save

description.p: Right-click the captions for settings. Drag them to move them.

NowCaption's own speech model: NVIDIA's model trained further on 3,100 hours of English speech. It makes fewer mistakes in meetings, calls, videos and noisy speech (13.7% of words against 15.0% on average), as quickly as before and on the same CPU. Also fixes for changing screens and for computers that cannot keep up with the speech. The Background filter has been removed: it still missed most words over music and made plain speech less accurate.

ul.li: Fewer word errors on everyday speech: meetings 21.1% instead of 24.5%, noisy speech 20.8% instead of 24.5%, business calls 17.2% instead of 20.0%
After Move to next screen, the captions still notice screens being plugged in or removed, and still fit the screen when its resolution or scaling changes
When recognition falls behind, captions skip ahead to live speech in one step instead of staying two seconds late and restarting many times a second
The Falling behind notice no longer says that 0.0 s of audio was skipped

description.p: NowCaption is English-only again: Translate to English has been removed. Copied and saved transcripts now keep the same punctuation as the captions on screen, including lines that have scrolled away.

ul.li: Saving to the same file twice in quick succession always keeps the newer transcript
A late error from a previous sound source can no longer interrupt recovery of the current one

description.p: Memory use no longer grows with the length of a session, and NowCaption uses about 15% less memory. Finished caption lines now go to a temporary file that only NowCaption can open and that is deleted when it quits, and memory it no longer needs is returned to the system. Captions, Copy and Save are unchanged.
Fixes a memory leak that made NowCaption use about 800 MB more memory for every hour of speech, reaching several gigabytes in a long session. Memory use now stays flat. Captions are unchanged.

Music-filter errors now turn the filter off while ordinary captions continue. Source changes keep buffered filter audio and settled punctuation. Audio and recognition warnings stay visible until recovery, and failed transcript exports release pending saves. Source setup now fetches the filter model and repairs broken Python environments after interpreter changes.
The right-click menu now stays open while you change the text size or background, so you can press − or + several times in a row and watch the captions change.

New: Filter out music, in the right-click menu. It picks out voices from music before recognition, so songs and speech over background music get many more words captioned. It is off by default because it uses a little more processor time and slightly lowers accuracy on plain speech.
Captions appear sooner: audio now reaches the speech model in smaller pieces, cutting the typical delay by 60 to 80 milliseconds with the same accuracy and processor use.

Settings that are out of range, for example after editing the settings file by hand, are corrected instead of giving an unreadable caption box. If the settings file cannot be saved, changes still apply until you quit, and switching the sound source keeps working.
NowCaption now runs on 64-bit ARM computers as well as x86_64. It can be installed from its own Flatpak repository, so new versions arrive with your other updates instead of being downloaded by hand.

Captions no longer jump around: punctuation in older lines stays as it was shown, so commas and full stops do not come and go and re-wrap the text. A large caption box now fills all its rows instead of stopping at two or three. The right-click menu opens on the first click on KDE Plasma.

The caption box can be resized: drag an edge or corner to make it wider, narrower or taller. The height snaps to whole rows, so a taller box shows more lines of captions. The size is remembered, and Reset size in the menu restores the default.

Recognition retries now back off correctly and cannot interrupt a recovered sound source. Notifications appear below live captions. Quit and window close wait for accepted transcript saves to finish, and failed saves keep the app open. Benchmark tracing now retains words after they scroll out of the caption window.

Model-loading failures can now be retried from the source menu. Recognition recovery preserves unfinished transcript text, and Clear discards buffered speech. Audio setup and shutdown run in the background, queued audio is bounded when recognition stalls, and captions resize when display resolution or scaling changes. Additional regression tests and corrected transcript and latency checks improve release verification.

More dependable captions. If the audio device disappears or the sound server restarts, NowCaption says so and reconnects by itself, and an error in speech recognition is reported and recovered from instead of silently stopping the captions. Copy and Save now include the words still being spoken and the whole session, Clear no longer lets old words come back, and saving reports whether it worked. Switching screens resizes the captions to fit.

Captions can now be dragged anywhere on the screen, and on KDE Plasma, Hyprland and Sway clicks outside them reach the windows underneath. Captions always show two lines, with punctuation that carries across pauses. The right-click menu is smaller and opens where you click, with one-row text size and background controls.
First release. Captions desktop audio or the microphone in English, with punctuation, adjustable text and a transcript you can copy or save.
